title: Putnam County, FL, 207 Diner cited for 15 violations during health inspection - NewsBreak
text: Popular local spot, 207 Diner, located at 101 W McCormick Road in East Palatka, Putnam County, FL, was cited for 15 violations during an August 7 inspection by the Florida Department of Business & Professional Regulation, requiring a follow-up inspection. State records showed that the restaurant, which holds a 4.4-star rating based on 512 Google reviews, was issued a warning but remains open for business before undergoing a follow-up review. The violations found during the initial inspection were categorized as three high-priority infractions, three intermediate violations, and nine basic violations. According to the inspector's note, high-priority violations included employees touching ready-to-eat food with bare hands without approved procedures, raw animal products stored above ready-to-eat items in freezers, and multiple food items held at temperatures exceeding 41 degrees Fahrenheit in the walk-in cooler. Temperature control was among the most notable issues during the inspection. Collard greens, potato salad, green beans, coleslaw, cooked cabbage, beans, chowder, and soup were all found stored between 46-49 degrees Fahrenheit in the malfunctioning walk-in cooler. The operator explained that the cooler was experiencing freezing issues, with maintenance installing a defrost timer set for 9 a.m., though kitchen staff frequently opened the door before that time to stock the line. Raw chicken was discovered stored above ready-to-eat gyro meat, while raw scallops sat above French fries in the reach-in freezer. An employee rearranged the storage levels, and the violation was corrected on-site. A staff member was also observed handling bread with their bare hands during food preparation without following approved alternative operating procedures. Meanwhile, intermediate violations included missing written procedures for bodily fluid cleanup and food debris on a can opener blade, marked as a repeat violation. Basic violations ranged from dead insects found in equipment to wet mops stored improperly and single-service items kept on the floor. The popular local diner, known for breakfast and homestyle dishes including meatloaf in a casual atmosphere, underwent a follow-up inspection on August 11, 2025, which saw all the previous infractions cleaned up, and the restaurant met inspection standards that same day. High Priority Violations: Please Share Your Thoughts: Please note that an inspection is one moment in time and not necessarily how a restaurant operates day to day.
